newsitem.title: UK: European directors quit troubled UK lobby firm.
newsitem.headline: European directors quit troubled UK lobby firm.

text.p: The directors of the European arm of a British lobbying firm at the centre of a row over parliamentary sleaze wracking the ruling Conservative Party announced they had resigned on Sunday.

Brad Staples, managing director of Ian Greer Europe, the Brussels-based subsidiary of Ian Greer Associates, said he and fellow directors Liam McArthur and Edward Walsh had been kept in the dark about the London office's activities.
Two British-based directors announced their resignations earlier on Sunday.
Ian Greer Associates (IGA), run by veteran lobbyist Ian Greer, is caught up in in a scandal over cash payments to members of parliament in return for their tabling questions in the House of Commons.

Confirming the resignations, Staples told Reuters: "The reason is that we were not fully informed of Mr Greer's financial relations with MPs in the UK. I no longer have confidence in Mr Greer's management."
Greer could not be reached for comment.
The resignations will mean the effective end of Ian Greer Europe and place a question mark over Greer's ambitions to expand business outside Britain following controversy at home.

Greer and Neil Hamilton, a Conservative former minister, were forced last week to drop a libel action against the Guardian newspaper, which had named them in connection with the cash-for-questions scandal.

Since then, the row has spiralled into a major embarrassment for the Conservatives as they prepare for their last annual conference ahead of a general election which Prime Minister John Major must call by next May.

Hamilton is to be probed by parliament's Commissioner For Standards, Sir Gordon Downey, following claims by Mohamed Al-Fayed, owner of London's Harrods store, that he paid the MP cash to table parliamentary questions.
Hamilton has admitted accepting 10,000 pounds ($15,600) from Greer, who has also made payments to campaign funds of a number of MPs from all three main parties. Most were Conservatives.
On Thursday, Lady Turner of Camden, a member of the IGA board, was sacked as the opposition Labour Party's employment spokeswoman in the unelected House of Lords after she defended Greer's actions.
Earlier on Sunday, two British-based directors of the firm announced their resignations.
Robbie MacDuff and Jonathan Hopkins, both long-time Labour Party members and trade unionists, accused Greer of withholding information concerning the scandal from them and other directors.
